blocks.text: An ordinary differential equation is an equation involving an unknown function of one independent variable and one or more of its derivatives. ODEs are used to describe quantities that change with respect to another variable, such as time, distance or position.

• An ODE is linear if the dependent variable and its derivatives occur only to the first power and are not

blocks.text: A separable differential equation can be rearranged so that all terms involving the dependent variable are on one side and all terms involving the independent variable are on the other.
• If dy/dx = f(x)g(y), rearrange to dy/g(y) = f(x) dx, then integrate both sides.
Example 4 — Separable equation with an initial condition
• Integrate: ln|y| = x² + C, so y = Ce^(x²).

blocks.text: An initial-value problem gives a differential equation together with a condition such as y(xn)=yn. The condition determines the arbitrary constant in the general solution.
• An ODE may describe a rate of change. For example, if y represents the amount of a quantity at time t,
then dy/dt represents its instantaneous rate of change. An initial condition specifies the starting state.

blocks.text: A common second-order linear homogeneous ODE has the form ay'' + by' + cy = 0, where a, b and c are constants. We use the characteristic equation to determine the form of the solution.
• Assume y=e^(rx). Substitution gives the characteristic equation ar²+br+c=0.
• If the roots are distinct real numbers rn and rn, then y=Cne^(rnx)+Cne^(rnx).
• If there is a repeated root r, then y=(Cn+Cnx)e^(rx).
